newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ING to up stake in Mendes Gans to 55 pct.
newsitem.headline: ING to up stake in Mendes Gans to 55 pct.

text.p: Dutch financial services giant Internationale Nederlanden Groep NV (ING) said on Monday it was close to buying the 20 percent shareholding in Mendes Gans currently owned by Chase Manhattan Bank.
This would bring ING's total shareholding in the small Dutch cash management bank to 55 percent, ING said.
"Both companies (ING and Chase Manhattan Bank) expect to reach agreement soon...Bank Mendes Gans will continue its operations independently under the current management," ING said in a statement.
Bank Mendes Gans offers integrated cash management systems and information systems to multinational companies. It is also active as an asset manager and offers investment administration systems.
Mendes Gans booked a net profit of 10.9 million guilders over 1995, compared with 10.5 million the year before.
In August Mendes Gans said net profit over the first six months of 1996 was 7.5 percent higher than in the year-ago period, but it gave no figures.
